And so hearing from the quality of life boards, understanding where their priorities lie, as we do uncover budget savings, making sure that we know where they can go, that every dollar has a place and that we know the value of those investments. If we're trying to save money, maybe on a big contract like what we discussed today, if we are going with a lower bidder, if we are trying to cut some budget, understanding what the benefit of that is when we're making that decision, understanding what the cost is if we go a different direction, I think is really important. So I'd love to see us open that up again to our boards and commissions without any dollar value attached for it, simply asking maybe for their top three and seeing what we get back and understanding those needs from our boards on the council level. Second, I think it's also time for our boards and commissions to discuss again, reviewing their founding resolutions and the board makeup, just to make sure that everything is good. I just like hearing from the boards every two to three years on that subject, seeing if there's anything that is either missing or anything that we'd like to edit or amend. We did it a couple of years ago. I'd just love to see us do that again. And frankly, that's a really good conversation to tie in with the potential grant program discussion, because they're prioritizing the things that they would like us to be able to budget and invest in, at the same time of talking about who they are as a board and what their makeup should be and all that stuff. So I'd love to be able to see those two things going to our boards. And finally, speaking of boards, the Trail Tunes musician applications are due by the end of the day on the 19th. I'd be remiss if I didn't mention that. If there's any Madison Heights residents watching this who either are a musician or know one, that time is running out to be able to perform at the festival. We've already had dozens of submissions from really phenomenal musicians. So if you want your shot at being able to play at the festival, definitely submit as soon as you can. Don't wait until the last minute and then accidentally miss it. Get that in right away. That's it,

This time was given to us last year when we had our last in-person meeting, and Vida Palazolo came, and we had a speaker talk a little bit about multiple sclerosis, because this is Awareness Month, and no one reached out to me or anyone on Council that I'm aware of, so I just want to take a minute just to sort of share a couple of statistics that people, or just a bit of information that people may not know about MS, but it's a disease of the central nervous system, and it's one where your immune system actually attacks the nerve cells, and it renders the patient unable to properly transmit information, so it causes imbalances, it can weaken your vision, it can cause fatigue, and a lot of other unpredictable symptoms, and right now there is no actual cure. There's a lot of effective treatment, and they are looking for a cure. I know several people in the City who have MS, and actually the first person I remember meeting who had MS was not in this City. It was someone I met when I was a teenager, and she was pretty young, and I didn't realize it, but apparently MS doesn't usually strike until you're in your 30s, so it's just something that can really get anyone at any time, so if you, you know, are so inclined, please go online, take a look, and find someday this month to wear orange to bring awareness, and then finally, I want to thank everybody who has reached out to our fire family and to the Brozich family to offer support. At the funeral, I had the opportunity to talk with some of our retired firefighters, really about how we can best honor our fallen hero, and it was just a really touching, it was a touching time.
